Definition: from G1909 and G1097; to know upon some mark, i.e. recognize; by implication, to become fully acquainted with, to acknowledge:--(ac-, have, take)know(-ledge, well), perceive.
BiblicalUsage: Epiginosko means to know fully, to recognise — to know upon some mark. Ye shall know them by their fruits; the disciples' eyes were opened and they knew Him; the council perceived that Peter and John had been with Jesus; and now we see through a glass darkly, but then face to face, and I shall know even as also I am known.
TheologicalSignificance: To know God is to be changed by Him, and the day is coming when I shall know Him as fully as He knows me. I believe this is the knowledge that saves: not knowing about Christ, but recognising Him — by His fruits, by His voice, by His presence.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Simon Peter; John the Apostle; Paul
